title: a `neural_block` descriptor carrying a populated, otherwise-valid `derivative` block is rejected — forbidden means populated
why: This fixture is row01's golden descriptor plus a valid-shaped `derivative`
block (a real primal reference, recompute-only policy, empty residuals —
exactly the shape a real derivative kernel like row01b carries). The
block's shape is deliberately correct so that the only rule that can
reject this fixture is the one under test: a descriptor forbids a
`derivative` block outright, regardless of whether the block itself would
separately pass its own shape check.
Forbidden means populated, consistently across all of the descriptor's
forbidden fields — an empty-string or empty-container form is treated as
absent and accepted (see row18b, this fixture's counterpart).
`derivative` is forbidden on the descriptor because it belongs on the
kernel the descriptor's `vjp_exec` names (row01b), not on the descriptor
The neural-specific checks run before the general derivative-shape check,
in both languages: this fixture's well-formed derivative block is what
proves that ordering, since a malformed block could not distinguish the
The manifest-bypassing plugin loader is exercised too, since its only
structural gate is the shared validator.
